decision: unkey's script stays in guest.ts beside identityScript, which reads the marker it leaves. The smolvm adapter decides when it runs and turns its ScriptFailed into Internal, so Runtime.capture keeps RoomError | StateError

decision: the smolvm adapter owns its parked bases and the host-key drop of a build's copy, and its make from a build's checkpoint forks the park and its startup the settle into the runtime Layer's scope, unawaited. Operations names none of them

evidence: commit d5f7dac; apps/host/src/platform/smolvm/smolvm.ts capture, startup, layerScope

decision: the base script a guest is prepared with is the Runtime port's guest, debian or macos, not a trait
why: which shell prepares a guest is the adapter's own fact. No rule and no client reads it

decision: the host config decodes in two stages, the common fields with runtime as an open record, then the one named runtime's settings through the registry. A config that still says kind is refused with a hint naming runtime
why: a Schema union over the registry would lose the per-runtime error and the kind hint

decision: placement judges what the control plane knows of a host, its drain and for a template's create whether it holds a copy, before its reply, so every host's reason comes through one path. NotBuilt advises a build only where one cures the miss, naming the template's file and the create's --host
why: a template create that named a host without a copy answered NotBuilt with no reason and advised a plain build, which put the next build on the old host again

decision: captureFrom is the one state, running or stopped, a runtime captures or forks a machine in
why: smolvm copies only a running machine and Tart only a stopped one, for a capture and a fork alike, so one trait says both

decision: an adopt gives a restarted host its machines. The host takes each handle from its ref or finds it by instance, reopens the relay of each that no step since has moved on, and answers each handle and endpoint, naming those whose search failed. The server writes the resolved rows at once and records the boot only once nothing is unresolved. The Runtime port has no adopt
why: smolvm and Tart implemented adopt as nothing, and one machine whose search failed kept every other row on its host without its handle and endpoint until it resolved
evidence: commits eefd6aa, 8dd01d5; apps/host/src/recheck.ts adopt; apps/server/src/fleet.ts adopted

decision: admission, capacity and a read take each machine's handle from its row and search only for one with none, each search on its own, so one that fails counts that machine unread, at its whole RAM, for admission, and reads it unknown
why: a search per held machine that failed as one let one machine's failed lookup fail every make, start, resize, capacity read and read on its host
evidence: commit eefd6aa; apps/host/src/operations.ts heldOf, heldBy, readAlone

decision: a make runs no search for its instance first, and each make, a capacity move's included, takes a new instance
why: a make step is entered only at a row's birth or by a capacity move, a delivery of the same ID returns that operation, and a lost make is undone, so no make of one instance is delivered twice. An instance then names one make on one host, so no row takes a retired instance again
evidence: commits eefd6aa, 64be263; apps/host/src/operations.ts made; apps/server/src/machines.ts born, movedOn

decision: a step's host is sent the rows that may hold a VM there, never one resting undone, with every row's port as taken
why: admission alone reads the machines, and an undone row's VM is deleted, so sending it would only cost a search

decision: Tart's find answers a machine's handle while its launchd plist or log is left, not only while Tart lists its VM
why: an undo sent again with no handle after its host died past tart delete found nothing and was done, leaking the job, its plist and its log. A runtime's find is its own account of what it keeps

decision: an operation's entry on the host keeps the refs its step names, not the step
why: keeping the step kept its setup script past the step

decision: NoOrphan stays an invariant, excusing a late landing, beside the temporal EventuallyNoOrphan
why: making NoOrphan temporal would weaken the configs that held it as an invariant. The narrower invariant keeps them exactly as strong

decision: Drifting.cfg runs one client, one fault and one host restart, MaxOps 9
why: adding a crash, a partition and a lost delivery passed 6.8M states in 10 minutes with the queue still growing

decision: a sweep deletes only the machine instances the store retired on that host, never anything for want of a claim. The store retires an instance in the write that ends its hold, when the row goes, moves host or instance, or rests undone or failed. Only machines are retired, and only a host whose runtime marks its machines is swept, waited for as long as the host says a sweep takes
why: a sweep by claims deleted wanted machines under clock skew, a coarse provider clock, a wiped or restored store and a second control plane. A retired instance is never wanted again, so a set any store read at any time is safe
evidence: commits 64be263, ffffcd1, 6fd29f8; apps/server/src/store.ts holdOf, ended; apps/server/src/fleet.ts swept, recheckHosts; apps/host/src/recheck.ts sweep

decision: a checkpoint a provider holds through its machine carries no mark of its own and is deleted only by a start or a remove of that machine, when keep lacks its handle. A sweep deletes a retired machine keeping every checkpoint it holds
why: only a step that owns the machine's lease runs beside no capture, so keep then holds every handle a row wants
evidence: commits 64be263, ffffcd1; apps/host/src/runtime.ts Owned; apps/host/src/recheck.ts swept

decision: a host lists what it marked only when the store retired something there
why: a list with nothing to delete is a billed call for nothing

decision: test:live is a vite.config.ts task with its cache off, not a package.json script
why: a cached script runs with the environment stripped, so the provider keys never reached the suite

decision: the smol cloud adapter's Layer provides Node's WebSocket constructor itself
why: the runtime registry's Layer takes only a spawner, files and an HTTP client, and the exec stream needs a WebSocket with headers

decision: the Sandbox Agent provider's destroy and pause end the machine's tunnel only once its delete or stop is done
why: the SDK resolves a session from its event stream before its own POST has read the reply and calls destroy then, so a tunnel cut there ended that read in an unhandled rejection that ended the process before the delete was sent

decision: a boat capture whose save answer was lost reads the snapshot by its name, goes on when it is there and fails with the lost answer when it is not, and never sends the save twice
why: an answer that leaves the outcome unknown is settled by reading the resource, and no probe showed what boat does with a save sent twice under one name

decision: boat's guest channel pins the host key /sshkey answers, and on a refused host key reads /sshkey again and runs the command once more
why: the identity script re-keys sshd between two execs of a first start, and the port has no path for the adapter to learn the key a guest script printed. A refused host key means the command never ran, so only that case runs again

decision: boat holds checkpoints through machines, and owned lists the sandboxes carrying the host's cbx-host label, each with the handles of the marked saved snapshots taken from it
why: a saved snapshot carries no label, so its only mark is its name and its source sandbox. Without owned, a create that lands after its undo runs with no expiry and bills until someone notices

decision: a base names boat's one image as ubuntu-24.04, and any other base a create names is a saved snapshot's name
why: boat boots one Ubuntu image and offers saved snapshots as templates, and a saved snapshot's name can hold no '.', so the two can't collide

decision: each boat type's disk is what the live suite read from the guest's root block device, 80 GiB on small and default and 149 GiB on large. xlarge keeps the docs' 251, as no account here offers it
why: boat's docs say 51 GB, which the guest contradicts

decision: a boat delete unsaves the sandbox's marked snapshots that keep lacks before it removes the sandbox and again once it is gone, and fails if a prune fails, so it runs again. A start whose prune fails logs it and still answers the running machine
why: a saved snapshot is reached only through its sandbox, and one saved while its sandbox is deleted stays listed past it, billed, with nothing to find it. A machine boat started runs whatever its prune does

decision: a retired record lasts a day from the first sweep that reached its host and left nothing of it. A sweep answers each retired instance it still lists, as a step names it or its delete failed, and those stay untold
why: a day from the retirement lost the record while a host was down or refusing, and a delete that failed but answered OK started the day of a resource still billed, leaving it with nothing to name it
evidence: commits 39d0a0b, 784b6b8; apps/server/src/fleet.ts retiredLast, swept; apps/server/src/platform/sqlite.ts retired told_at

decision: AnswerTrue under Drifting.cfg excuses only an answer that the machine runs while a drift is unread, and only an answer that the machine is gone while a late VM waits for its sweep

evidence: commit dcf8b88; .agents/skills/verify-machine-answers/model/MachineAnswers.tla AnswerTrue; Drifting.cfg fails AnswerTrue with no excuse

decision: ssh and ssh-proxy, the SSH config's ProxyCommand, give up on an endpoint that hasn't connected and sent its banner within 15 s of the dial. The SSH config sets no ConnectTimeout
why: a relayed endpoint whose host is frozen takes the connection and sends nothing, which hung ssh-proxy for good. ConnectTimeout runs from the proxy's start and would end ssh naming no machine while the proxy still reads
evidence: commit de133be; packages/sdk/src/ssh.ts sshAnswersWithin; apps/cli/src/ssh.ts; apps/cli/src/ssh-config.ts

decision: a mutation's timeout bounds its reply and its wait together, by one deadline taken when it begins
why: a timeout bounded the wait alone, so a capture whose host can't be read took the host read's 10 s plus the 20 s asked

decision: the control plane's journal is the host's, one middleware in the host contract, which logs a 500 or an undeclared failure at error, a request cut short by its client or the stop not at all, and every other answer at debug
why: a 404, each client abort and each request the stop cut logged an 18-line error, and two copies of what must log no secret would drift

decision: the client and the control plane's call to a host turn an HTTP client defect back into the failure it is, so a page at a status an action declares is read as an answer
why: effect 4.1.3's HttpApiClient combines a declared status's error with its body's decode failure, and Cause.combine hashes the Node response, whose jsonUnsafe getter throws on a body that isn't JSON, so the call died. Both catchDefects go once effect stops hashing the response

decision: ssh and the SSH config clankerbox keeps set ServerAliveInterval 30 and ServerAliveCountMax 4
why: nothing bounded an endpoint silent after its banner. 15 and 3 cut a logged-in session about a minute into an outage, so these give a session the two minutes a wait gives an outage. The provider's tunnel keeps a shorter check of its own

decision: the journal logs a request's path, not its URL
why: http.url carried the query string, which a caller may send a secret in as in a body

decision: boat's Idempotency-Key names the host and the instance, cbx-<host id>-<instance>, not the bare instance
why: two hosts of one account, or two control planes, making one instance would send one key with two bodies, which boat refuses 409 idempotency_key_reused

decision: the boat adapter's snapshot mark is cbx- and 32 hex digits, and the list asks namePrefix=cbx-
why: a saved snapshot carries no labels, so its name is its only mark, and the bare prefix cbx- pruned a snapshot someone named cbx- by hand

decision: boat's saved-snapshot list is read whole, not paged
why: boat's API refuses limit and cursor there with 400 invalid_query, takes only name, namePrefix and org, and answers no pageInfo

decision: a boat host refuses to start on an SSH key, or a key folder, open to its group or others, and makes a new key 0600 in a 0700 folder
why: OpenSSH refuses such a key at every command, and tightening it silently would hide that the key may have leaked

decision: a provider list decodes each record alone, and one the host can't read fails the list only when it carries this host's mark. Each mark is read on its own
why: the lists are account-wide, so one malformed record of another tenant failed every list, check and sweep, and an odd field read as no mark at all

decision: a smol cloud exec's stdin is sized by its JSON encoding against the request body's 1 MiB, inline when the body fits and staged in pieces otherwise
why: smol cloud answers 413 past 1 MiB of request body, and a stdin of control characters or quotes under 1 MiB raw passed it encoded

decision: a boat create or fork whose answer was lost is looked for by its labels before it is sent again, and one boat holds idempotency_in_progress is waited for by its listing, never sent again
why: boat counts a start for each create it refuses idempotency_in_progress, against an hourly limit the account's hosts share

decision: provider-http.ts owns the rules both rented clients keep, which are each request's bound by what it asks (answerWithin, 30 s a read, 1 min a change, 5 min a settle), the sends after a lost answer, the read until a resource rests and the step bound, and the lint fence lets only a provider's client import it
why: each client kept its own counts and loops, so one bound drifted from the other, and a stalled connection held its step for ever
evidence: commit 3506bed; apps/host/src/platform/provider-http.ts answerWithin, triesAfterLoss, untilRest, bounded; oxlint.config.ts

decision: a smol cloud 422 other than machine size exceeds is Capacity only when the account, read after it, holds the machines its limits allow, and Internal otherwise
why: smol cloud answers schema errors 422 too, and the wording of a limit refusal is not known, so matching words moved creates on a config error

decision: a provider record the host can't read is named in a log line or an error by its name or ID alone, or as a record with none, and nothing else of a provider's answer reaches either
why: the whole record was the label, so a record carrying a token put it in the host's log
evidence: commits 2f5eb59, 3506bed; apps/host/src/platform/provider-http.ts recordReader; apps/host/src/platform/smol-cloud/api.ts label; apps/host/src/platform/boat/api.ts label

decision: a smol cloud 409 is waited out and the machine read again, and a 409 three times in a row while the machine stays in one settled state fails WrongState with the provider's reason, over asking again until the step's ten minutes run out
why: smol cloud answers 409 both to a machine on its way and to a request it will not take in the state the machine rests in; only a refusal that stands across reads of a resting machine is the second, and asking on lost its reason
evidence: commit fbbfb571; apps/host/src/platform/smol-cloud/smol-cloud.ts standingAfter; apps/host/tests/platform/smol-cloud.test.ts refused 409 while the machine stays where it was
